answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a marble, before it can post or attest. Forging 500 aliases hence costs 159 bonds held for 17 days each, plus the wander attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single horizon checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
